_comment: Skirmish map recipes (docs/13 section 5). A map is a list of feature specs, not a list of features: the actual placement is drawn from the battle seed so a replay reproduces the map along with everything else. short is what fits on a picker card at the bitmap face's fixed size; name is what everything with room says. Ranges are inclusive [min, max]; count is how many groups, cluster is how many bodies per group, body is the collision radius and field is the effect radius, both in arena units. variants, where a kind has them, is the list of looks a feature may wear; which one is drawn comes from the battle seed like everything else, so a replay shows the same world. moons is how many companions a body keeps, moon_size is their radius as a fraction of its own, and moon_orbit is how far out they sit as a fraction of its well; a moon is the same kind of feature with no well of its own. Adding a map type, or a new kind of world, is an entry here, never code (CLAUDE.md 5.4).

open.name: Open Space
open.blurb: Nothing but the two of you. Range and arcs decide it.

nebula.name: Nebula Shoals
nebula.blurb: Ionised cloud banks. Sensors lose lock through the thick of it, and so do theirs.

belt.name: Debris Belt
belt.blurb: Loose rock in dust halos, strewn wide. Crossing fast strips a shield; crossing into one ends worse.

orbit.name: High Orbit
orbit.blurb: One world, off centre, with what it has caught. The well pulls, and the surface does not forgive.
